source.title: Neural networks with late-phase weights
source.authors: Johannes von Oswald; Seijin Kobayashi; J. Sacramento; Alexander Meulemans; Christian Henning; B. Grewe

record.tranche_reason: The paper compares dropout with a baseline and measures a weight-perturbation flatness score alongside generalization, using different conditions and metrics from the mapped versions.
record.gate_note: Late-phase-weight results and comparisons with other methods are not rows unless they measure a mapped claim version. The paper reports no random-label, width-sweep, architecture-comparison, optimizer, batch-size, or memorized-example-removal result. Flatness results are included as a related measurement, but do not establish the specific V7 relationship.
record.test_reason: The dropout comparisons test V6 in WRN image classifiers. The gradient-accumulation controls also test V5: increasing the effective batch size tenfold late in training lowers test accuracy under the same data and epoch budget.
record.authors_conclusion: The paraphrase is broadly accurate: appropriately chosen late-phase weights improve generalization across the tested image and language benchmarks, and the CIFAR-100 BatchNorm variant has lower perturbation sensitivity. The dropout comparisons show inconsistent accuracy benefits, although dropout is not a central conclusion.
record.recipe_differences: The paper evaluates late-phase weight training and related methods; it does not reproduce the original methods mapped in the claim versions. Its dropout comparison uses a WRN 28-10 on CIFAR-100.
record.method_sensitivity: Dropout probability changes the test-accuracy outcome (p=0.1, 0.2, 0.3).

fits_no_version.finding: Late-phase BatchNorm weights improve test accuracy and reduce relative loss sensitivity to multiplicative weight noise.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: In this WRN CIFAR-100 comparison, late-phase BatchNorm training improves test accuracy and produces lower relative loss increases under magnitude-scaled Gaussian perturbations.

record.problems: The flatness comparison is figure-only and the text does not provide numeric scores; the compared CIFAR-100 models have different final training losses. Dropout test-accuracy differences are small for p=0.1 and p=0.2, and no significance test is reported.
record.rows_left_out: No additional results on mapped versions were reported. Late-phase-weight accuracy results, OOD measures, and other method comparisons do not measure the behaviors named by the versions. Dropout MC-dropout results were left out because the V6 claim concerns adding dropout, and the paper reports the direct dropout sweep in Table 13.

untested.parts: Random-label memorization and its comparison with natural-label generalization.
Width sweeps beyond the width required for zero training error.
Convolutional versus fully connected architectures and learned local connectivity.
Adaptive versus SGD optimizer comparisons under different tuning budgets.
Language models, batch-size threshold sweeps, longer training, warmup, and normalization or regularization remedies.
Fully connected classifiers, very small training sets, demonstrated underfitting from excessive dropout, and joint removal of dropout and weight decay.
Ranking generalization gaps among similarly fitted networks and comparison with norm- and margin-based measures.
Removing memorized training examples and comparing with random removal.

missing.what: Direct CIFAR-10 dropout comparison: base accuracy 96.16±0.12%, dropout p=0.2 accuracy 96.02±0.06%, five seeds. Dropout probability was tuned only on CIFAR-100.
missing.locator: Section 3.2, Table 1; Appendix B, Related work

missing.what: Effective large-batch controls: accumulate over ten minibatches beginning at epoch 120, otherwise retain the base training setup and data budget. Base accuracy is 81.35±0.16%; summed-gradient control is 80.76±0.26%; averaged-gradient control is 80.34±0.28%, five seeds.
missing.locator: Appendix B, Gradient accumulation control, Table 10; Section 3.2

record.verdict_notes: The study is not an original source for these versions. V6 is conditional, so failures at particular dropout settings limit its scope rather than refute its claim of benefits in some regimes. MC-dropout results are explicitly declared omitted in the record.

versions.untested_parts: Random-label fitting and held-out natural-label performance.
Large versus small batch generalization under epoch budgets.
Fully connected classifiers, other datasets, very small training sets, and removal of dropout together with weight decay under data augmentation.

The paper measures a magnitude-scaled perturbation flatness score, but does not compare networks at similarly low training loss or test whether the measure ranks generalization gaps better than norm- and margin-based measures.

rows.subject: WRN 28-10 with BatchNorm late-phase weights
rows.operation_detail: Measure loss increase under multiplicative Gaussian weight perturbations scaled to each weight.
rows.measure: Flatness score δL/L under multiplicative Gaussian weight noise
rows.note: The text says the score increases more slowly with σz for late-phase BatchNorm models, but does not report numerical values. Training losses differ between the compared models.
rows.check: The figure establishes a slower increase in relative loss under magnitude-scaled noise, but does not measure V7's generalization-gap ranking. CIFAR-100 training losses also differ substantially: 0.0024 versus 0.0267.
